$comment: Fixed points with seeded placement, GAME_DESIGN.md section 9. Hollowbrook is always at the origin. The Hall and the standing stones are placed at seeded angles inside a distance band, always on ground flat enough to build on. Landmarks.ts searches the band with the world RNG and never calls Math.random.

village.name: Hollowbrook
village.$comment: Terrain.ts already flattens a plateau here, so no search is needed.
village.$comment_walls: Spacing between wall-ring collider spheres, Structures.ts. Tighter than the Hall's 3m step because a house wall run is a fraction of the Hall's length, and a coarse step there would leave corner-sized gaps on a building this small.
village.$comment_home: House index 0's furniture, marking it as the player's home for the wake-up scene a later milestone spawns into. Offsets are local to that house's own frame (front at -z, same convention as the door anchors in models.json).

hall.name: The Meadows Hall
hall.$comment: The building is axis-aligned to its own yaw. Interior is one room, entry at -z, Bracken at +z, four alcoves down the long walls.
hall.$road: The road stub points back toward the village so a player who finds the Hall from any direction has a thread to follow home, and a player following the road from the village arrives at the door.

$search: Both searched landmarks sample candidate angles from the seeded RNG and take the first that clears maxSlope and sits above the waterline. If no candidate in `attempts` qualifies, the flattest seen wins, so world generation always terminates with a placement.
